faq.healthIdQ: How do I show my Health ID at a facility?
faq.healthIdA: Open the Health ID tab. It shows your Health ID and a QR code the facility can scan. You can also generate a temporary QR code that expires, when you would rather not share the permanent one.
faq.whoSeesQ: Who can see my medical record?
faq.whoSeesA: Only the facilities you have granted consent to. You approve or revoke each request under Privacy & consent, and every access to your record is written to your access history.
faq.copyQ: How do I get a copy of my records?
faq.copyA: Download my records exports your medical record as a PDF to read or print, or as a FHIR file for another system. For a formal data export, raise a request under Data requests.
faq.offlineQ: Can I use OpesCare without a connection?
faq.offlineA: Yes, if you turn on offline access. It keeps a limited, encrypted copy on this device — profile, upcoming appointments, medications, allergies and your emergency profile — and tells you when it was last refreshed.
faq.bookingQ: How do I book an appointment?
faq.bookingA: Choose a facility, pick a date, and book one of the slots it has published. Your upcoming and past appointments are listed under Appointments, where you can also cancel one.
faq.familyQ: Can I manage a relative’s record?
faq.familyA: You can invite a relative to link their record to yours, or register a dependent such as a child. Both are under Family, and an invitation can be cancelled while it is still pending.

under `opesDoctor`, together with the identical-keyed fr file, then delete both.
This is a DELTA, not a catalogue. Everything the clinician messaging + profile
slice needed at ship time was already in the locale files — including the
i18next plural forms messages.waiting_one/_other and
profile.experienceYears_one/_other, and a whole photo vocabulary
(profile.photo, changePhoto, addPhoto, photoFailedTitle, photoCheckHint).
The refined 'missing route vs refused conversation' branch in messages.tsx
and messages/[id].tsx reuses opesCore.errors.* rather than adding keys.
Two things are left, and `corrections` is the important half.
1. `corrections` — copy already in the catalogue that the SERVER has since
made untrue. Overwrite the existing values with these.
profile.photoDesktopOnly currently says the photo can only be changed
from the desktop system. That was true when it was written and is not
any more: POST /api/mobile/doctor/profile/photo is live, validated and
rate-limited. The string is not referenced by any screen today, so
nothing on screen is wrong yet — but the next person to wire a photo
control would reach for it and ship a false statement.
profile.photoInvalid says 'smaller than 5 MB'. The server's cap is
4 MB (max:4096 KB), so the app would be promising an allowance the
API refuses. The number here matches the server.
2. `additions` — the only genuinely new keys: picking a source, and the two
refusals the server can give that no existing string covers.
photoNotAnImage       <- PHOTO_NOT_AN_IMAGE (422): the bytes are not a
JPEG/PNG/WebP, whatever the file was named or
what Content-Type the client claimed.
photoDimensionsTooBig <- PHOTO_DIMENSIONS_REJECTED (422): a small file
that decodes to an enormous image.
Why the photo control is not built: the app bundles no image picker, and
adding expo-image-picker is a package.json change — package.json is shared
with the other agents working this repo. app/clinician/profile.tsx already
renders an existing photo_url; only the control to change it is missing.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lede: OpesCare Finder holds medical information about you. This page explains, in plain words, what the app collects, who can see it, and what you can do about it. It describes what the app actually does today — not what it might do later.
privacy.collectIdentity: Identity and contact details you give us: your name, date of birth, sex, phone number, email address, postal address, and the name and phone number of the emergency contact you nominate. If you register a dependent, we collect the same details for them.
privacy.collectHealth: Health information held in your OpesCare record: your Health ID, blood group, allergies, diagnoses and conditions, immunisations, prescriptions, laboratory orders and results, vital signs, care plans, referrals, appointments, and clinical documents issued to you.
privacy.collectUsage: Requests you make in the app: appointment bookings and cancellations, medicine reservations, blood requests, laboratory test requests, messages you send to your care team, support tickets, and any free-text note or reason you type into them.
privacy.collectDevice: A device identifier the app generates for itself — a random string, not your hardware serial number and not an advertising ID. It lets us tie a notification registration and an offline-access authorisation to this handset, and nothing else.
privacy.locationWhen: The app asks for location only while you are using it, and only on the screens that need it. It never tracks you in the background.
privacy.locationBlood: In Blood Finder, your coordinates are sent to our server so it can rank blood banks by real distance from you. This is the only place your precise position leaves the device.
privacy.locationMap: On the Care Map, your coordinates stay on the device. They are used to sort nearby facilities and to work out how far away each one is. The app converts your position into a city name and sends only that city name to filter the directory.
privacy.locationDecline: You can decline location entirely. Both screens then fall back to a city you choose from a list, and everything else in them keeps working.
privacy.useCare: To give you and the clinicians you authorise a single, accurate view of your health record across the facilities you visit, so your care does not restart from nothing at every door.
privacy.useOperate: To operate the features you ask for: finding medicines and blood in stock, booking appointments, issuing your Health ID, and delivering the copies of your record that you export.
privacy.useSafety: To keep the platform safe and accountable: authenticating you, preventing abuse, and recording who opened your record so you can audit it.
privacy.useLegal: To meet obligations that apply to health records under the law of the country where your care is delivered.
privacy.neverSell: We do not sell your personal or health information, and we never have.
privacy.neverAds: We do not use your information for advertising, and the app carries no advertising.
privacy.neverTrack: The app contains no analytics, tracking, attribution or crash-reporting service of any kind. It talks to one server — ours — and to no other company. Nothing you do in the app is reported to a third party.
privacy.sharingTitle: Who else can see your record
privacy.sharingConsent: A health facility or clinician sees your record only within a consent you granted. You approve or refuse each request in the app, you can see every consent that is currently active, and you can revoke any of them at any time.
privacy.sharingLogs: Every access is logged. Privacy › Access log shows you who opened your record, when, from where, and for what stated purpose — including any emergency access.
privacy.sharingPrescription: When you share a prescription with a pharmacy, the app creates a limited, expiring link that shows that prescription and nothing else. You can revoke it before it expires.
privacy.sharingFamily: If you invite a family member, they see only what the access level you chose allows. You can withdraw that access.
privacy.storageTransit: Everything the app sends travels over an encrypted HTTPS connection.
privacy.storageDevice: On your phone, your session token and any offline copy of your record are held in the operating system's secure store — the iOS Keychain or the Android Keystore — which is encrypted at rest and tied to your device unlock.
privacy.storageOffline: Offline access is off until you switch it on, and it stores only the categories you approve: your demographics, upcoming appointments, medications, allergies, and an emergency profile. You can erase that copy from the device at any time in Settings › Offline access. The authorisation itself expires on its own within 24 hours.
privacy.storageWeb: If you use OpesCare in a web browser rather than the installed app, browser storage offers no encryption at rest. The app warns you before it stores anything there.
privacy.rightsSee: See your record: every clinical section in the app is your own data, shown to you in full.
privacy.rightsExport: Take a copy: Settings › Download my records exports your record as a PDF or as a FHIR R4 bundle you can hand to any other system.
privacy.rightsCorrect: Correct it: if something in your record is wrong, Privacy › Data requests raises a correction request against the specific entry. Clinical records are never silently overwritten — a correction is recorded as an amendment, which is what makes the history trustworthy.
privacy.rightsRevoke: Withdraw consent: revoke any facility's access from the Privacy screen, at any time, without giving a reason.
privacy.rightsDelete: Delete your account: the app cannot yet do this for you. Email us at the address below from the address on your account and we will close it and delete the personal data we are not legally required to retain. Medical records that a facility is obliged by law to keep are retained by that facility, and we will tell you which ones those are.
privacy.childrenBody: The app is intended for adults. A parent or guardian may hold a dependent's record through the Family feature, and is responsible for that child's information in the app. We do not knowingly let a child create an account for themselves.
privacy.changesBody: If we change what we collect or what we do with it, we will update this page and the date shown at the top of it, and — where the change is significant — tell you in the app before it takes effect.
privacy.contactBody: Questions about this policy, or a request about your data — including deleting your account — go to:

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.lede: These terms cover your use of the OpesCare Finder app. The first two sections are the ones that matter most to your safety — please read them even if you read nothing else.
terms.emergencyTitle: This app is not emergency care
terms.emergencyBody: If you are having a medical emergency, stop and call your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department. Do not use this app to seek urgent help. Messages, appointment requests and blood requests are not monitored continuously and may not be seen in time.
terms.adviceTitle: It does not give medical advice
terms.adviceBody: OpesCare Finder shows you information from your health record and from the facilities in the national directory. It does not diagnose, treat, or tell you what to do about your health. Nothing in the app replaces a consultation with a qualified clinician, and no result, value or flag shown here should be acted on without one.
terms.adviceResults: Laboratory results and vital signs are shown as your facility reported them. A reference range or an out-of-range marker is a laboratory's own annotation, not an interpretation of what it means for you.
terms.accountTruthful: You must give accurate identity details. Your Health ID is issued against them, and a record attached to wrong details is a danger to you: it can put someone else's allergies or blood group in front of the person treating you.
terms.accountSecurity: Keep your password, PIN and one-time codes to yourself. Anyone who signs in as you can read your entire medical record. Tell us immediately if you think someone else has access.
terms.accountOne: One account belongs to one person. Use the Family feature to hold a dependent's record rather than sharing a login.
terms.accountClosing: You may close your account at any time by writing to us. The app cannot yet close it for you; the Privacy Policy explains what happens to your data when you do.
terms.availabilityReported: Medicine stock, blood availability and appointment slots are reported to OpesCare by the pharmacies, blood banks and facilities themselves. We publish what they tell us, with the time it was last updated. We do not hold the stock, and we cannot guarantee that an item shown as available still is when you arrive. Call ahead when it matters.
terms.availabilityReservation: A reservation is a request to a pharmacy, not a purchase. The app takes no payment. You pay the pharmacy directly, at the pharmacy.
terms.availabilityBlood: OpesCare takes no payment for blood, and a blood request placed here is a request to a blood bank — it is not a guarantee that units will be held for you.
terms.availabilityAppointment: An appointment booked in the app is confirmed by the facility, and the facility's own rules on lateness, cancellation and fees apply.
terms.recordSource: Your record is written by the clinicians and facilities that treat you. OpesCare carries it between them; it does not author it.
terms.recordAmend: Clinical entries are never silently overwritten. If something is wrong, you can raise a correction request against that entry, and the change is recorded as an amendment with its history intact. That is what makes the record safe to rely on.
terms.recordConsent: You control who sees your record. Access is granted by your consent, is limited to what that consent covers, and is logged so you can check it.
terms.acceptableBody: Do not use the app to impersonate anyone, to access a record that is not yours or lawfully shared with you, to place false blood or medicine requests, or to disrupt the service for others. Do not attempt to break, probe or circumvent its security. We may suspend an account that does.
terms.liabilityUptime: We work to keep the service available, but we do not promise it will be uninterrupted or error-free. Maintenance, network failures and the systems of the facilities we connect to can all interrupt it.
terms.liabilityThird: Where the app shows information supplied by a facility, a pharmacy, a blood bank or a laboratory, that party is responsible for its accuracy.
terms.liabilityExtent: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss arising from your reliance on information the app displays where that information came from a third party, or from your use of the app in place of professional medical care.
terms.changesBody: We may update these terms. When we do, we will change the date at the top of this page, and tell you in the app before a significant change takes effect. Continuing to use the app after that means you accept the updated terms.

messagingRecipients.facilityHint: The front desk answers opening hours, booking, results and whether a medicine is in stock.

messagingRecipients.facilityNoneTitle: No facility to write to yet

consentPrompt.laterHint: You can still answer from Privacy & Data.
consentPrompt.approved: {{facility}} now has access. You can withdraw it at any time from Privacy & Data.
consentPrompt.denied: Request from {{facility}} denied. Nothing was shared.
consentPrompt.failed: That did not go through. Nothing has changed on your record. Try again.

requests.declinedBody: The patient will see your reason.
requests.failedHint: Refresh the requests — if this one is no longer listed as pending, the decision was recorded.

order.title: Lab order
order.notServedBody: This order cannot be opened until the lab desk is enabled for this app.
order.missingBody: This screen was opened without an order. Go back to the queue and open one.

order.collectBody: {{test}} for {{patient}}. The order moves to Awaiting results.
order.collectedBody: The order is now awaiting results.
order.collectFailedHint: Open this order again — if it shows as collected, it was recorded.

order.savedBody_other: {{count}} result rows were added. They are not yet visible to the patient or the clinician — release when the report is complete.
order.saveFailedHint: Open this order again — rows that were recorded will be listed under Results.
order.releaseCaption: Releasing notifies the patient and the ordering clinician and cannot be undone.
order.releaseNeedsResults: Enter at least one result before releasing.

order.releaseBody_other:

order.releaseFailedHint: Open this order again — if it shows as Resulted, the release was recorded.
order.releasedCardBody: The patient and the ordering clinician were notified when these results were released. Nothing further can be changed here.
order.offTrackBody: No laboratory action applies to it on this desk.
order.roleCollectOnly: Your role can collect samples here; entering and releasing results is not part of it.

entry.title: New results

entry.flagHint: Optional. H high · L low · N normal · C critical — your call, not the phone’s.
entry.notesPlaceholder: Anything the clinician should know about this value
entry.fixRows: Complete the highlighted rows before saving.
entry.saveHint: Saving adds these rows to the order. Nothing is released until you press Release.

home.title: Pharmacy desk
home.subtitle: Dispensing, orders and stock
home.footer: Every figure is counted by the server for your pharmacy. Dispensing is recorded under your name; charts are not part of this desk.

lookup.title: Dispense by Health ID
lookup.label: Health ID
lookup.invalid: Enter the full Health ID — at least {{min}} characters, letters, digits and dashes only. This desk cannot search by name.
lookup.noNameSearch: No name search: an exact Health ID from the patient’s card or code is the only way in. Only prescriptions dispensable at this pharmacy are returned.
lookup.noAnswerTitle: Nothing came back for that Health ID
lookup.noAnswerBody: Either no record carries {{healthId}}, or this server does not serve the pharmacy desk yet — both answer the same way, so this screen will not tell you which. Check the ID against the patient’s card and try again.
lookup.emptyBody: {{healthId}} has no active prescription that can be dispensed at this pharmacy. This says nothing about prescriptions held elsewhere.
lookup.noPatientTitle: No one holds this Health ID
lookup.noPatientBody: {{healthId}} is not on record. Check the card or code with the patient — a typo is the usual cause.

queueEmpty.incomingBody: Nothing has been routed to this pharmacy that you have not yet accepted.
queueEmpty.preparingBody: Accept an incoming prescription to start preparing it.
queueEmpty.readyBody: Mark a prepared prescription ready and it will wait here for the patient.
queueEmpty.dispensedBody: Prescriptions dispensed at this pharmacy will be listed here.

reservationsEmpty.title: No orders: {{status}}
reservationsEmpty.body: Medicine orders in this state will be listed here as patients place them.

reservationConfirm.readyBody: {{medicine}} for {{patient}}. The patient is told it is ready.
reservationConfirm.collectedBody: {{patient}} has collected {{medicine}} at the counter. This closes the order.
reservationConfirm.dispatchBody: {{medicine}} for {{patient}} leaves the pharmacy for the delivery address. The patient is told.
reservationConfirm.deliveredBody: {{medicine}} has reached {{patient}}. This closes the order.
reservationConfirm.cancelBody: {{medicine}} for {{patient}} will be cancelled and the patient will read your reason. This cannot be undone.

prescription.title: Prescription
prescription.notInListsBody: This prescription is not in any queue this desk has read. Open it again from the queue or from a Health ID lookup.
prescription.leftQueueTitle: This prescription has left the queue it was listed in
prescription.leftQueueBody: What you see is the last copy this desk read. Pull down to re-read, or go back to the desk.
prescription.identityOnly: Name and Health ID identify the patient. Their chart is not part of the pharmacy desk.
prescription.noItems: The prescriber listed no medicines on this prescription.

prescription.readyBody: {{patient}} is told their medicines are ready for collection.
prescription.dispensedBody: This prescription has been dispensed at this pharmacy. Nothing more to do here.

prescription.footer: Accepting, marking ready and dispensing are recorded under your name at this pharmacy.

dispense.notesPlaceholder: Substitution, counselling given, anything the record should carry
dispense.skipHint: Only the lines with a quantity above 0 are recorded as dispensed.

reservation.title: Order
reservation.notInListsBody: This order is not in any list this desk has read. Open it again from the Orders queue.
reservation.leftListTitle: This order has left the list it was in
reservation.leftListBody: What you see is the last copy this desk read. Pull down to re-read, or go back to the desk.
reservation.closedBody: This order is closed. Nothing more to do here.
reservation.footer: Every step is recorded under your name and the patient is told on their phone.

cancel.title: Cancel this order
cancel.intro: The patient reads this reason on their phone. Say plainly why — out of stock, prescription needed, expired hold.
cancel.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Out of stock until Thursday
cancel.reasonRequired: Give the patient a reason of at least a few words.

stock.title: Stock

stock.summaryWithLow_other: {{count}} lines · {{low}} at or under reorder level

stock.emptyLowBody: Every line is above its reorder level.

adjust.title: Adjust stock
adjust.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Delivery received, count correction, expired batch removed
adjust.belowZero: That would take the shelf below zero.
adjust.reasonRequired: Give a reason of at least a few words — it goes on the stock movement.
adjust.audit: Recorded as a stock movement under your name. The shelf figure only changes once the server confirms.
adjust.checkHint: Re-open the shelf — if the quantity has changed, the movement was recorded. If not, adjust it again.

write.refusedBody: The server refused what was entered. Nothing was changed.
write.checkQueue: Open the queue again — if the prescription has moved, it was recorded. If not, try again or use the web counter.

errors.goneTitle: This appointment is no longer here

book.emptyFilteredBody: The book has rows for this day, but none with this status or clinician.

appointment.noShowMessage: {{patient}} — {{type}} on {{date}} at {{time}}. Closes the appointment and records that the patient did not attend.

A healthier Africa.
